newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH C.BANK APPROVES LICENCE FOR VOLKSBANK BRNO.
newsitem.headline: CZECH C.BANK APPROVES LICENCE FOR VOLKSBANK BRNO.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB), the country's central bank, said on Tuesday that it had approved a request for a banking licence for Volksbank a.s., based in the Czech second city Brno.
Volksbank officials in Brno said that with the new licence, the bank will be able to function as a full universal bank.
Until now, the bank, whose parent is Oesterreichische Volksbanken AG , has had permission only to function as a branch.

"In the last year, we submitted a request to the central bank to transform into a joint-stock company. We were expecting a positive result (to this)," Karel Platl, deputy director of the Brno operation.
The central bank said in a statement that the licence would become valid as of January 1, 1997 and that "Volksbank a.s. will operate with basic capital of 500 million crowns as a universal bank".
